answer: Trust-graph routing mitigates Sybil attacks by scoring nodes via random walks over verified peer connections. Instead of letting a zephyr of cheap bots sway decisions, the protocol isolates attackers behind topological bottlenecks. Gaining influence demands the verifiable cost of securing authentic trust edges from the honest node grove, preventing fake identities from spreading like wild yarrow. A key limitation is that honest newcomers lacking social ties suffer severe cold-start rejection.
